title: Adaptive reservation estimator and noise-attribution pilot for dedicated pools
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Summary: After a capacity incident on dedicated-gpu-pool-7 where multiple tenants experienced intermittent tail latency and a small wave of evictions, we traced the immediate trigger to an under-provisioned static reservation for several tenants combined with a short-lived noisy workload that exhausted the KV cache and pushed kernel scheduling into a less-efficient path. This ticket scopes a 6-week pilot to (1) build an adaptive reservation estimator that recommends reservation sizes based on tenant fingerprints and recent traffic patterns, (2) deploy a noisy-neighbor attribution pipeline so we can quickly identify which tenant(s) caused noisy bursts, and (3) prototype a smoother burst policy with token-bucket decay and hysteresis to avoid oscillatory evictions.
impact_summary: ~35 tenants across 4 clusters saw 95th/99th token latency regressions for 10-15 minutes; two low-priority tenants experienced soft evictions. Customer-facing impact: low to medium (non-critical timeouts for internal integrations). Internal impact: increased paging and on-call load; confidence hit in reservation sizing guidance.
root_cause_summary: Combination of factors: static reservation sizing conservative for steady-state but not adaptive to bursty arrivals; lack of per-tenant KV cache pressure telemetry; existing burst policy uses an aggressive instantaneous credit model that caused hard handoffs when multiple tenants spiked simultaneously.
proposed_work_items: W1: Data pipeline - ingest per-tenant request histograms (p50/p95/p99), token churn, and KV cache miss rates; store 14d sliding window (owner: SRE - PR #infra/2789)
W2: Estimator - implement adaptive reservation estimator service that suggests reservation-size-percentiles (50/90/99) and confidence; include feature flags for canary (owner: infra-allocator)
W3: Attribution - add noisy-neighbor scoring (burst-index) derived from request spectral analysis and cache eviction causality; surface top-3 suspects in Console alert (owner: telemetry)
W4: Burst policy - replace instantaneous credit refill with token-bucket + exponential decay hysteresis; add per-tenant soft-fence to avoid oscillation (owner: serving-runtime)
W5: Safety and rollout - implement stage gating with synthetic tenants and canary clusters, add automated rollback on eviction-rate regressions (owner: reliability)

W6: Runbook & dashboards - update dedicated capacity runbook, add one-click mitigation in Console (isolate tenant, scale temporary reservation), dashboard panels for reservation drift and burst-index (owner: ops)
W7: Post-deploy evaluation - run 2-week A/B between static and adaptive reservations, measure unit cost, tail latency, and eviction frequency (owner: data-science)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Telemetry only (2 weeks) - enable per-tenant metrics and verify data quality in staging
Phase 1: Estimator canary (2 weeks) - serve estimator suggestions in read-only mode in Console; collect feedback and match against historical incidents
Phase 2: Attribution + Alerts (1 week) - enable noisy-neighbor scoring and trigger Slack alerts to on-call with suspects
Phase 3: Burst policy canary (2 weeks) - enable token-bucket burst policy in 5% of dedicated clusters with synthetic traffic
Phase 4: Gradual rollout (2-4 weeks) - expand to remaining clusters with automated rollback thresholds for eviction spikes and median latency regressions
